originalTitle: Spamhaus new email sender requirements in November
content:
Starting in November 2026 , we are gradually rolling out a requirement for every sending IP to have a valid HELO, a reverse DNS (PTR) record, and a matching A record. Use the HELO checker below to see whether the DNS meets our best practices, and follow the guidelines to avoid being listed.

Guidance for senders, mail admins, and postmasters on meeting Spamhaus's sending requirements. All senders must meet these minimum email sending requirements to avoid being listed.

Each recipient should confirm their address by clicking a link in a confirmation email. If no confirmation is received, do not send email to that address. Purchased, rented and harvested lists are the most common source of spam trap hits, and hitting traps is one of the fastest routes to a listing. See section

Publish forward-confirmed reverse DNS for every sending IP

Every sending IP must have a reverse DNS entry pointing to a fully qualified domain name (FQDN). That hostname must, in turn, resolve back to the same sending IP address. This is known as forward-confirmed reverse DNS (FCrDNS). An IP with missing or mismatched reverse DNS is treated as suspicious and is one of the most common reasons for an IP to be considered for listing. See section

Use a HELO/EHLO hostname that resolves to the sending IP

The hostname the server announces in the HELO/EHLO command must resolve to the IP it is connecting from, and must stay consistent across connections from that IP. Placeholder values, hosting-provider defaults, and hostnames that vary between connections are treated as signals of misconfiguration or compromise and can result in a listing. See section

Meet the IPv6 allocation and reverse DNS minimum

If sending over IPv6, the sending address must fall within an allocation of /64 or larger (a /64 is the standard block size we recommend assigning), and that space must have valid reverse DNS. IPv6 ranges without reverse DNS or with allocations smaller than /64 are often misused by spammers. See section

Authenticate mail with SPF , DKIM and DMARC

Publish SPF and DMARC records for every sending domain, sign every outbound message with a signature, and align the DKIM sending domain with the domain in the message's RFC 5322 From address. Authentication is one of the signals that shapes reputation, so gaps here make a listing more likely when other signals are weak. See section

All sending infrastructure must have the following DNS and mailserver configuration. Failure to do so can result in IPs being listed on the Email Spam IPs (CSS) or compromised IPs (XBL) zones.

Ensure the sending IP address has a valid reverse DNS (rDNS) entry resolving to a fully qualified domain name (FQDN) for the sending IP address. Spamhaus will treat emails originating from IP addresses without rDNS as suspicious and this will be reflected in the IP's reputation, and receivers using Spamhaus data may subject it to additional filtering.

Ensure the rDNS hostname resolves to the connecting IP address via a corresponding forward DNS (A/AAAA) record .

Abusive actors often rely on the reputation of upstream DNS records to hide their identity. Instead, configure a branded reverse DNS to use the sender's own domain, to improve trust signals for the IP address.

Do not use generic or auto-generated rDNS entries for dedicated IPs that point to the hosting provider (e.g., static-203-0-113-25.hosting.example.net , 203.113.0.25.broadband.example.net , vps-25.dedicated.hosting.example.com etc). These can negatively impact reputation.

Do not use random dictionary words in the rDNS and make it identifiable to the sending infrastructure.

Use the Spamhaus DNS checker tool to check your rDNS configuration.

Ensure the hostname used in the HELO/EHLO command resolves to the sending IP address.

Maintain a consistent HELO value that resolves to the sending IP address. Multiple HELO values resolving to different IP addresses may indicate residential proxy and/or malware behaviour.

Where possible, ensure the HELO/EHLO hostname is consistent with the rDNS hostname.

Host a webpage on the domain of the HELO, that explains what the domain is for, or that redirects to the main brand domain.

Do not use placeholder values such as localhost or generic hostnames that point to the hosting company/ISP as the HELO value.

Do not resolve HELO hostname to infrastructure that is not used for sending — this behaviour is associated with spoofing and misconfiguration.

Do not use generic or auto-generated names provided by the hosting provider, use the sender's own domain where possible.

Do not impersonate the HELO value of well-known mailbox providers like Gmail or Hotmail.

Enter an IP address into the Spamhaus DNS Checker at the top of this page , to check its HELO value. An email can also be sent to helocheck@abuseat.org to check the HELO being used.

IPv6 customer allocations must be at least /64 and must have valid reverse DNS. The /64 minimum is consistent with IPv6 subnet architecture and RFC 6177 's guidance that email senders should be able to obtain at least a /64. This is further discussed in M3AAWG best practices for IPv6 allocation.

Add routes for all IP space owned by the sender to reduce vulnerability to BGP hijacking , which can allow hackers to send email that appears to originate from the IP space.

Run dig -x to confirm reverse DNS is present. To confirm the space is actually routed, look the address up at bgp.he.net .

Make sure SPF is set up correctly for the domain used in the envelope sender ( RFC 5321 MAIL FROM), and points to the sending infrastructure.

Use SRS (Sender Rewriting Scheme) to rewrite the envelope From (MAIL FROM) if mail is forwarded, so SPF can still be checked against the forwarding domain.

Do not allow freemail addresses such as gmail.com or hotmail.com as the 'Envelope FROM.'

Do not use the NULL envelope sender <> for anything other than indirect out-of-band delivery reports, DSNs and MDNs.

chineseTitle: Spamhaus 11 月新电子邮件发件人要求
chineseContent:
从 2026 年 11 月开始，我们逐步要求每个发送 IP 都具有有效的 HELO、反向 DNS (PTR) 记录和匹配的 A 记录。使用下面的 HELO 检查器查看 DNS 是否符合我们的最佳实践，并遵循指南以避免被列出。

为发件人、邮件管理员和邮政局长提供满足 Spamhaus 发送要求的指南。所有发件人必须满足这些最低电子邮件发送要求，以避免被列出。

每个收件人应通过单击确认电子邮件中的链接来确认其地址。如果未收到确认，请勿向该地址发送电子邮件。购买、租用和收获的列表是垃圾邮件陷阱命中的最常见来源，而命中陷阱是到达列表的最快途径之一。参见部分

为每个发送 IP 发布前向确认的反向 DNS

每个发送 IP 必须有一个指向完全限定域名 (FQDN) 的反向 DNS 条目。该主机名必须依次解析回相同的发送 IP 地址。这称为前向确认反向 DNS (FCrDNS)。反向 DNS 丢失或不匹配的 IP 被视为可疑，并且是考虑列出 IP 的最常见原因之一。参见部分

使用解析为发送 IP 的 HELO/EHLO 主机名

服务器在 HELO/EHLO 命令中宣布的主机名必须解析为它所连接的 IP，并且必须在来自该 IP 的连接之间保持一致。连接之间不同的占位符值、托管提供商默认值和主机名被视为配置错误或妥协的信号，并可能导致列表。参见部分

满足 IPv6 分配和反向 DNS 最低要求

如果通过 IPv6 发送，发送地址必须位于 /64 或更大的分配范围内（/64 是我们建议分配的标准块大小），并且该空间必须具有有效的反向 DNS。没有反向 DNS 或分配小于 /64 的 IPv6 范围经常被垃圾邮件发送者滥用。参见部分

使用 SPF、DKIM 和 DMARC 验证邮件

发布每个发送域的 SPF 和 DMARC 记录，使用签名对每个出站邮件进行签名，并将 DKIM 发送域与邮件的 RFC 5322 发件人地址中的域对齐。身份验证是塑造声誉的信号之一，因此当其他信号较弱时，此处的差距会使列表更有可能出现。参见部分

所有发送基础设施必须具有以下 DNS 和邮件服务器配置。如果不这样做，可能会导致 IP 被列在垃圾邮件 IP (CSS) 或受损 IP (XBL) 区域中。

确保发送 IP 地址具有解析为发送 IP 地址的完全限定域名 (FQDN) 的有效反向 DNS (rDNS) 条目。 Spamhaus 会将来自没有 rDNS 的 IP 地址的电子邮件视为可疑，这将反映在 IP 的声誉中，并且使用 Spamhaus 数据的接收者可能会对其进行额外的过滤。

确保 rDNS 主机名通过相应的转发 DNS (A/AAAA) 记录解析为连接 IP 地址。

滥用行为者通常依靠上游 DNS 记录的声誉来隐藏自己的身份。相反，配置品牌反向 DNS 以使用发件人自己的域，以改善 IP 地址的信任信号。

不要对指向托管提供商的专用 IP 使用通用或自动生成的 rDNS 条目（例如 static-203-0-113-25.hosting.example.net 、 203.113.0.25.broadband.example.net 、 vps-25.dedicated.hosting.example.com 等）。这些会对声誉产生负面影响。

不要在 rDNS 中使用随机字典单词，并使其能够被发送基础设施识别。

使用 Spamhaus DNS 检查器工具检查您的 rDNS 配置。

确保 HELO/EHLO 命令中使用的主机名解析为发送 IP 地址。

保持解析为发送 IP 地址的一致 HELO 值。解析到不同 IP 地址的多个 HELO 值可能表明住宅代理和/或恶意软件行为。

如果可能，请确保 HELO/EHLO 主机名与 rDNS 主机名一致。

在 HELO 域上托管一个网页，解释该域的用途，或重定向到主品牌域。

请勿使用占位符值（例如 localhost 或指向托管公司/ISP 的通用主机名）作为 HELO 值。

不要将 HELO 主机名解析为不用于发送的基础设施 - 此行为与欺骗和错误配置相关。

不要使用托管提供商提供的通用名称或自动生成的名称，尽可能使用发件人自己的域。

请勿冒充 Gmail 或 Hotmail 等知名邮箱提供商的 HELO 值。

在本页顶部的 Spamhaus DNS 检查器中输入 IP 地址，以检查其 HELO 值。还可以发送电子邮件至 helocheck@abuseat.org 以检查正在使用的 HELO。

IPv6 客户分配必须至少为 /64，并且必须具有有效的反向 DNS。 /64 最小值与 IPv6 子网体系结构和 RFC 6177 的指导一致，即电子邮件发件人应能够至少获得 /64。 M3AAWG IPv6 分配最佳实践对此进行了进一步讨论。

为发件人拥有的所有 IP 空间添加路由，以减少 BGP 劫持的漏洞，这可能允许黑客发送看似源自 IP 空间的电子邮件。

运行 dig -x 以确认反向 DNS 是否存在。要确认空间确实已路由，请在 bgp.he.net 上查找地址。

确保为信封发件人 (RFC 5321 MAIL FROM) 中使用的域正确设置 SPF，并指向发送基础结构。

如果转发邮件，请使用SRS（发件人重写方案）重写信封From（MAIL FROM），因此仍然可以根据转发域检查SPF。

请勿允许免费邮件地址（例如 gmail.com 或 hotmail.com）作为“信封发件人”。

除了间接带外传送报告、DSN 和 MDN 之外，请勿将 NULL 信封发件人 <> 使用。

接受后不要发送退回邮件
